## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
`status()` should be fixed to show the same 12-character revision as `history()` and `completed()`: its docstring promises the same identifier, but the code truncates to 7 characters, and the added test does not check the revision.

## Changes
The pull request adds `status(revision, attempt)` and `attempt_label(attempt)` to `app/display.py` to render a "Running" status line with the revision and attempt number, plus an unused `REVIEW_HINT` string constant. It adds two tests in `tests/test_display.py`.

## Critical
(none)

## Important
- app/display.py:14 — correctness — Truncate the status revision to 12 characters like history — For revision `0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567`, `status()` returns `Running: 0123456 (attempt 2)` while `history()` returns `History: 0123456789ab`. The docstring says "using the same identifier as history", but the code uses `revision[:7]` where `history()` and `completed()` use `revision[:12]`. — An operator who matches the running status identifier against history or completion output finds no exact match for the same deployment. — Fix: Use `revision[:12]` and extend `test_running_status_contains_attempt` to assert the full status string, since it currently checks only the prefix and suffix.
